## Defensibility

**What is defensible now:**

- **Algorithmic novelty** — gradient-level shortcut detection is a new direction; ShortcutScore + gradient surgery are original contributions
- **Benchmark depth** — 13 methods x 5 datasets x full ablation; hardest comparison set in this subfield
- **Production-grade infra** — one-command reproduction, Optuna search, MLflow tracking, dual-scale profiles; not notebook-grade

**What strengthens the moat over time:**

- Proprietary shortcut taxonomy across domains
- Integration partnerships with MLOps platforms
- Enterprise deployment data → feedback loop (more failure modes → better detection)

---

## Engineering Stack = Business Value

| Property | Implementation | Business Value |
|----------|---------------|---------------|
| **Reproducibility** | One-command runs, seed control, config-driven | Audit trail for compliance |
| **Scalability** | Local / server profiles, SLURM support | Laptop to cluster, no rewrite |
| **Tracking** | MLflow + Optuna Bayesian search | No lost experiments |
| **Modularity** | 13 methods, common interface | New methods plug in via 1 function |
| **Documentation** | Quarto site, method docs, guides | Engineer onboarding in days |

---

## Risks

| Risk | Severity | Mitigation |
|------|----------|-----------|
| Gradient computation expensive at billion-param scale | **High** | Gradient sketching implemented; further approximations planned |
| ShortcutScore may not generalize to all shortcut types | Medium | Validated on 5 datasets with different structures |
| Buyers may prefer simpler approaches | Medium | Position as complementary — finds what simpler methods miss |
| Foundation model providers solve robustness internally | Medium | Unlikely near-term; active open research problem |
| Single-author dependency | **High** | Modular codebase, full docs, structured for team contribution |

::: {.callout-warning}
**Honest assessment:** The core algorithm is publishable and reproducible. A well-resourced team could re-implement it. The moat is in execution speed, benchmark depth, and domain-specific tuning — not secrecy.
:::
